country.name: Somalia
country.currency_notes: USD is also widely used in commercial transactions; Somaliland uses the Somaliland shilling in its own markets. Preserve the currency and territory context of every price observation.

purpose: Country evidence inventory for later crop- and livelihood-specific enterprise budgets. Not a calculator input file and not authority to activate the country.

evidence_sections.topic: seasonal cereal output and drought exposure
evidence_sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Somalia Country Brief, reference date 11 March 2026

observations.finding: Estimated lowest output on historical record, about 75% below the already-low average of the previous five years.
About 4% above the five-year average, because the major 2025 Gu harvest was well above average despite the very poor Deyr harvest.

observations.unit: percent of annual cereal output approximately
observations.finding: The secondary Deyr harvest in central and southern regions typically accounts for about 40% of annual cereal output.
Major Gu crops harvested in July 2025 in central and southern regions were well above average after abundant and well-distributed rainfall.

caveats: The aggregate annual cereal total masks major seasonal and geographic differences; it must not be treated as a stable farm yield.
The 2025 Deyr figure is an estimate for maize and sorghum, not an annual crop-specific national series.
The brief reports drought, conflict and water/pasture constraints that can sharply change yields and livestock productivity.

evidence_sections.source_name: Somalia Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation, National Food Security Updates
evidence_sections.reference_date: 2024 Gu season figures reported on ministry page; accessed 2026-11-01

observations.finding: Includes 14,100 tonnes of off-season production in late September/October 2024; reported 45% below the 2019–2023 long-term average.
Reported 62% below the 2010–2023 average, attributed to poor and erratic rainfall, dry spells and pests.

caveats: The ministry page gives regional aggregate cereal figures; it does not provide crop-specific area and yield in the page summary.
Southern and northwest geographic coverage should be retained as reported and not conflated with a single countrywide Gu total.

evidence_sections.source_name: Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit (FSNAU), Agriculture methodology

observations.finding: Gu crop season is generally April to June; Deyr crop season is generally October to December.
Parts of Awdal and Woqooyi Galbeed produce rainfed maize and sorghum, alongside livestock herding.
A coastal cowpea belt is identified in central and southern Somalia.
Rainfed and irrigated maize are produced in the riverine valleys, with sesame as a cash crop.
Rainfed sorghum production is integrated with livestock production.
FSNAU states domestic production meets roughly half of population cereal requirements.

caveats: These are broad livelihood and agroecological zones, not a complete current crop suitability map.
Riverine irrigation access, rainfall, insecurity and seasonal conditions vary within each zone.

observations.finding: FSNAU states it conducts seasonal crop production surveys from 1995 to current, covering crop-producing districts.
The district estimates include cereal type, planted area in hectares and production in metric tonnes; yield can be derived as production divided by area when compatible denominators are supplied.

observations.item: Agricultural wage and cereal price monitoring
observations.finding: Cereal market prices and agricultural wage rates are collected weekly in 36 major markets.

caveats: The methodology page establishes dataset availability, not the actual latest district-level values. Download the relevant Gu/Deyr datasets and validate their coverage and metadata before creating calculator parameters.
Do not derive yield where planted area and harvested area definitions differ or where the same crop has multiple seasons.

evidence_sections.topic: weekly market price data and coverage
evidence_sections.source_name: FSNAU Market Price Monitoring System methodology

observations.finding: Weekly price monitoring covers cereals, other foods, livestock, energy and labour.
FSNAU reports market price data and exchange-rate series available from 1997 to current, including Somali and Somaliland shillings.
Monthly Market Data Updates include retail prices per kg and wholesale prices per 50 kg bag for sorghum, maize and rice.

caveats: Market retail and wholesale prices are not farmgate prices; they are useful for market context and cross-checking only.
Territorial currency differences, market location, product grade and price unit must be preserved.

evidence_sections.source_name: World Bank Microdata Library, Monthly food price estimates by product and market, version 2026-10-05
evidence_sections.reference_date: dataset version 5 October 2026; coverage 1 January 2007–1 October 2026

observations.finding: Selected estimates include camel and goat livestock, maize, milk, oil, rice, sorghum, wheat and wheat flour.
Weekly updated estimates combine direct price measurements with machine-learning imputation of missing observations, using WFP, FAO and selected national statistical sources.

caveats: The dataset includes modelled estimates and is intended to illuminate local food price movements where direct measurement is incomplete.
These are food market prices, not a verified producer farmgate price series; identify the raw-source flag and product unit before use.
The latest dataset end date in this catalogue version is 1 October 2026, not a live quote.

evidence_sections.topic: livestock production, drought and household income
evidence_sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Somalia Country Brief and FSNAU livelihoods methodology
evidence_sections.reference_date: FAO brief 11 March 2026; FSNAU methodology accessed 2026-11-01

observations.finding: Failed 2025 Deyr rains caused pasture and water shortages in central and northern pastoral areas; animal body condition deteriorated and livestock deaths from starvation and disease increased during the January–March 2026 Jilaal dry season.
FAO reports milk production at very low levels during the early 2026 drought period, reducing household food and income.
FSNAU reports pastoralists rely on local and export livestock sales and livestock products for 40–80% of cash income.

caveats: Livestock enterprise budgets require species, breed, herd structure, mortality, feed/water access, veterinary, migration and market data.
A drought-period assessment must not be generalized into a normal-year production assumption.

evidence_sections.topic: agricultural and livestock contribution to the wider economy
evidence_sections.source_name: IMF Somalia Third Review under the Extended Credit Facility

observations.finding: IMF estimated 2024 growth at 4%, supported by robust agricultural and livestock output after ample 2023Q4 and 2024Q1 rainfall.
Strong livestock exports in response to regional demand contributed to the 2024 current-account context.

caveats: Macroeconomic growth and export context do not provide crop-specific farmgate prices, yields or production costs.
The IMF figures are historical macro indicators, not current calculator input prices.

evidence_sections.topic: 2026 Gu season production outlook, drought impacts, market-price monitoring and 2026 market bulletin evidence
evidence_sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Somalia Country Brief; FEWS NET Somalia Food Security Outlook Update; FSNAU agriculture methodology; M-TACAB Suuq Bulletin
evidence_sections.reference_date: FAO GIEWS brief 15 September 2026; FEWS NET August 2026 update; M-TACAB bulletin issue 04 published 4 October 2026; reviewed 4 November 2026

observations.finding: FAO reports below-average and erratically distributed April–June rainfall, crop wilting and stunting, and severe drought affecting 25–70% of cropland in mid-June in Lower/Middle Shabelle and the Bay sorghum belt. Improved late Gu and July Xagaa rains supported partial recovery in some areas. Aggregate 2026 Gu and off-season cereal production remained uncertain pending FSNAU production estimates as of 15 September 2026.

FEWS NET's August 2026 update describes mixed outcomes: better performance in some southeastern riverine and agropastoral areas, below-average production in pump-irrigated Hiiraan and Gedo and parts of Bay, Gedo and Lower Juba, and exceptionally poor harvests in parts of Bakool, Gedo and Hiiraan. This is a livelihood-zone assessment, not a full numeric crop-yield table.

FAO reports sorghum prices in Baidoa and maize prices in Qorioley rose between January and June 2026 by about 25% and 70%, respectively, then fell in July after the Gu harvest by about 10% and 30%. July prices remained around twice year-earlier levels. In Mogadishu, sorghum and maize rose 15–20% January–June, then eased 5–10% in July while remaining 25–45% above year-earlier levels. These are cereal market-price movements, not producer farmgate quotations.

FAO reports Mogadishu diesel prices increased 65% from January to April 2026, then declined around 25% by July but remained approximately 25% above the prior year. The September brief identifies high pump-irrigation fuel costs and low river levels as constraints on off-season production.

observations.item: FSNAU district-season data and wage series
observations.finding: FSNAU describes district crop production estimates for Gu and Deyr seasons from 1995 to current, including crop production, area and yield by district, and weekly cereal prices and agricultural wage rates in 36 markets. The methodology confirms the data series exist; the current underlying numeric datasets still need to be downloaded and checked.

The M-TACAB newsroom lists a 4 October 2026 bulletin with 672 daily price observations across Afgooye, Baidoa and Bakaaro. Earlier issues also report daily observations. The newsroom page was reachable in search results but its PDF download could not be inspected in this review, so no specific price values are copied into the evidence record.

caveats: FAO's 15 September 2026 brief explicitly says aggregate 2026 Gu and off-season production estimates were still pending; do not invent or extrapolate a final national crop total.
FEWS NET livelihood-zone qualitative findings do not substitute for district crop-area, production and yield tables.
FAO market-price changes and M-TACAB market bulletins are market evidence; do not label them farmgate prices unless transaction point is explicitly established.
M-TACAB issue 04 has 672 records according to its newsroom description, but values were not independently inspected; keep as a data acquisition lead only.
Pump-irrigation costs and fuel volatility vary by location, river level and season; obtain dated supplier and farmer quotations.

evidence_sections.topic: regional crop output, seed market pricing, 2026 retail price observations and updated market-data coverage
evidence_sections.source_name: Somalia National Transformation Plan 2025–2029; Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation/TASAI Somalia Seed Market Analysis and Somalia Country Report 2025; World Bank RTFP; WFP monthly market prices via HDX
evidence_sections.reference_date: 2023 crop production table published in NTP 2025–2029; seed prices refer to 2024 planting season; market datasets updated Aug–Oct 2026; reviewed 2026-11-05

observations.finding: Regional totals are presented as South, Northwest, Northeast and Central. Preserve the source's regional grouping and do not map these labels to administrative regions without a crosswalk.
The national planning report gives production by broad region; zero in the table should be treated as a reported estimate, not proof that no individual farms produced maize.
Sesame production is concentrated in South and Central in the published table.
Cowpea has a different regional pattern from maize and sorghum; regional commodity defaults must not be uniform.
Ministry seed-market study covered Southwest, Hirshabelle, Jubaland and Mogadishu; its sample is valuable for seed-system evidence but not a national farm census.
Seed prices are retail agro-dealer/company-level planting-season prices; grain prices are comparison market prices. They are not seed rates, per-hectare input budgets or farmgate output prices.
Eighteen active companies producing certified seed for major crops were reported; informal/uncertified seed sales remain material and regulatory coverage is incomplete.

observations.period: monthly data through August 2026; imported 21 October 2026
observations.finding: Published market prices are monthly retail observations and distinguish Somali shilling (SOS) and Somaliland shilling (SLS). The August 2026 snapshot is not a current live quote and is not farmgate.

The catalogue describes 10,948 cases and 116 variables, including market geography, currency, dates, direct and modelled price estimates. Preserve confidence and interpolation flags; these are food-market price estimates, not verified producer prices.

caveats: National Transformation Plan regional production table is for 2023 and does not provide planted/harvested area, crop-specific yield or district detail in the accessible extract.
The broad South, Northwest, Northeast and Central groupings require a documented crosswalk before populating the calculator's region selector.
TASAI seed prices are historical 2024 USD/kg observations. They are not 2026 quotations and do not replace seed-rate, delivery, variety and farmer-paid cost data.
WFP and World Bank price datasets are market-level retail/food-price estimates, not farmgate prices; SOS and SLS are not interchangeable.
Somalia's 2026 crop outcomes remain highly seasonal and spatially variable; 2025/26 drought evidence prevents using one national average yield as a safe default.

evidence_sections.topic: current calculator readiness and outstanding evidence requirements

observations.finding: Evidence is stronger for crop mix, 2023 broad-region production, 2024 seed prices and 2026 retail market monitoring. It remains insufficient for validated crop-by-district yields, current farmgate prices and complete enterprise budgets.

At minimum, retain irrigated Shabelle/Juba riverine maize and sesame; rainfed maize/sorghum; Bay-Bakool sorghum-livestock; coastal cowpea; and northwest rainfed maize/sorghum as separate production systems where local data permit.
Maintain SOS for Somalia observations, SLS for Somaliland observations, and USD only where explicitly quoted. Record territory, date and conversion source; do not merge price series.

caveats: No calculator activation, formula change, or deployment is authorized by this evidence refresh.

The 2023 crop production table, 2024 seed prices and 2026 market observations represent different periods and transaction levels; they must not be blended into a single current price/yield assumption.

calculator_data_gaps: Extract FSNAU seasonal Gu and Deyr district crop production datasets, including crop-specific area, production and yield, and retain season, district, survey method and year.

Obtain and inspect M-TACAB Suuq Bulletin issue 04 (12–25 September 2026; 672 observations) and subsequent bulletins; record actual product, market, date, unit, currency, grade and wholesale/retail/producer transaction type. Do not assume market observations are farmgate.
Reconcile and validate the Ministry of Agriculture March 2025 farmgate price table: clarify unit/quantity basis, SOS notation, market locations and unusually large figures before using any values.
Download weekly FSNAU market price and wage data for selected crops and target markets; keep wholesale and retail series separate from farmgate series.
Extract World Bank 45-market monthly estimates and preserve direct-observation versus machine-learning-imputed status, product units and subnational geography.
Collect current producer prices for maize, sorghum, sesame, cowpea, banana, mango, watermelon, onion and other regionally relevant crops.
Obtain current input quotations for seed, fertiliser, pesticides, irrigation fuel/pumping, labour, land preparation, transport and post-harvest handling by region and season.
Build distinct irrigated riverine, rainfed cereal, cowpea and sesame enterprise budgets; do not apply one national yield or cost profile across agroecological zones.
For livestock models, collect species-specific purchase prices, herd composition, feed/water, veterinary costs, mortality, milk yield, liveweight and export-market transaction data.

Clarify the geographic and currency treatment of Somalia, Somaliland and other administered territories; do not combine SOS, Somaliland shillings and USD without explicit conversion dates and sources.
Use FAO's 15 September 2026 seasonal brief as a drought/market context update only; it states that 2026 Gu and off-season aggregate cereal estimates remain uncertain pending FSNAU release.
Extract FSNAU crop data portal records by district, season, crop and year, including planted/harvested area where available; reconcile them with the 2023 national-plan broad-region totals.
Obtain current 2026 farmgate/producer transaction prices by crop, district, grade, unit and date; WFP/World Bank retail and modelled market estimates cannot substitute.
Obtain 2026 seed quotations and local delivery costs; retain the 2024 TASAI USD/kg values as historical benchmarks only and add seeding rates by crop/variety.
Obtain farmer-paid fertilizer, crop protection, irrigation/pump fuel, water, labour, land preparation, machinery, transport and post-harvest costs by production system.
Build tested regional enterprise budgets using separate irrigated riverine, rainfed cereal, cowpea and sesame systems, then add relevant livestock budgets.

activation_blockers: Current district-season crop area, production and yield series have not yet been extracted and validated; FAO's September 2026 brief says aggregate 2026 Gu/off-season production estimates were pending.
Ministry March 2025 farmgate price observations have unresolved unit and currency-scale anomalies.
New M-TACAB September 2026 market bulletin identified but its actual price records not inspected; market observations need transaction-point classification.
No complete region-specific crop enterprise budgets or current input quotations, including pump-irrigation fuel and labour.
Market datasets largely describe wholesale/retail or modelled food prices rather than verified farmgate prices.
Livestock systems require separate species- and livelihood-specific budgets.
Territorial currency and market coverage need explicit handling.
The 2023 national-plan crop table is broad-region production only; district crop areas and yields remain to be extracted and reconciled.
TASAI seed prices are 2024 planting-season USD/kg benchmarks, not 2026 complete input-cost schedules.
August 2026 WFP prices and October 2026 World Bank estimates are market/retail data, not verified farmgate prices.

safeguards: Research-only evidence; not a live calculator dataset.
Do not activate Somalia or change calculator formulas based on this file.
Do not treat FAO seasonal aggregate cereal output as crop yield or farm-level production.
Do not substitute wholesale/retail market prices, imputed food-price estimates or export values for farmgate producer prices.
Do not normalize suspicious SOS figures until their original quantity and currency basis is verified.
Keep Somalia and Somaliland market/currency observations explicitly labelled by geography.
